name: Symmetry Preference Ratings
description: Faithful replication of Bertamini, Rampone, Makin and Jessop (2019), PeerJ, "Symmetry preference in shapes, faces, flowers and landscapes", with the authors' greyscale stimuli from OSF 9qz6p. Ten items per category (landscapes, flowers, angular polygons, smooth polygons) exist as an original image and as a version mirrored to perfect vertical symmetry. Each participant sees one version of each item (version A: even items symmetrical, odd items original; version B the reverse; assigned at random), so 40 images. Part 1: rate the beauty of each image (1–100 slider, random order). Part 2: rate how obvious or salient the symmetry is in each image (same images, new random order). Part 3: speeded discrimination, 40 original/symmetrical pairs side by side, choose the more symmetrical one with the A / L keys or by tapping; choice, accuracy and response time are recorded. Finally an open question on strategy. Image keys (e.g. l2sl, f3v) and the version letter match catlia_data.csv on OSF, so new samples can be analysed with the authors' data. Main finding to compare: symmetry raised beauty for shapes and faces, but original landscapes were preferred to symmetrical ones. About 15 minutes. Differences from the original study: (1) the male and female face sets are not included (shared only on request from Rhodes et al.), so 40 instead of 60 images per part; (2) online with sliders instead of a lab PsychoPy rating scale (values 1–100 as in the open data); (3) tapping is allowed as well as the keys, and response time starts when both images have loaded; (4) age is asked. Stimuli used with credit to the authors (no licence stated on OSF); the template will be removed if the authors object.

Stimuli: Bertamini, Rampone, Makin & Jessop (2019), OSF project 9qz6p (landscapes from web images marked free to use; flowers after Hůla & Flegr 2016), used with credit to the authors and removed on request. The face set of the original study is not included.

config.description: Does making a landscape, a flower or a shape perfectly symmetrical make it more beautiful? Each of 40 greyscale images (landscapes, flowers, angular and smooth shapes) is shown either in its original form or mirrored to perfect vertical symmetry. Participants rate the beauty of each image, then how salient its symmetry is, then pick the more symmetrical image of each original/symmetrical pair as fast as they can. Rebuilt from Bertamini, Rampone, Makin and Jessop (2019), PeerJ, with the authors' stimuli from OSF 9qz6p.
